subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Quantum Tunneling: The Shrinking Limit
description: A short lesson to help you apply Quantum Tunneling: The Shrinking Limit.

hook.text: Shrink a transistor gate thin enough and electrons walk through it like a ghost through a wall.

buildup.text: Quantum tunneling lets electrons bypass barriers that classical physics says should stop them.

discovery.text: Below about 1 nm gate oxide thickness, tunneling current becomes unacceptable.

twist.text: High-k dielectrics replace silicon dioxide — thicker physically but thinner electrically.

climax.text: Hafnium oxide, introduced at 45 nm, solved the tunneling crisis and kept scaling alive.

punchline.text: When electrons start tunneling, engineers change the wall material instead.

quiz.question: How did engineers solve the quantum tunneling problem in thin gate oxides?
options: They made transistors larger to avoid thin gates
They replaced silicon dioxide with high-k materials like hafnium oxide
They lowered the operating voltage to zero
